story: Rama, an avatar of the god Vishnu, was born to King Dasharatha and his wife Kausalya in Ayodhya, capital of the kingdom of Kosala. His half-brothers were Lakshmana, Bharata, and Shatrughna. At a ceremony in the kingdom of Mithila, King Janaka offered his daughter Sita in marriage to whoever could string the great bow of the god Shiva. Rama alone succeeded, breaking the bow, and won Sita as his wife. On the journey home another avatar, Parashurama, challenged him to string the bow of Vishnu; Rama did so successfully and was acknowledged as a form of Vishnu. Rama and Sita lived happily for twelve years until Kaikeyi, another wife of Dasharatha, invoked an old promise and demanded that Rama be exiled for fourteen years. Rama accepted his father's word, and Sita and Lakshmana joined him in exile. They crossed a river and stayed at a hermitage with the sage Vasishtha, where a devotee named Shabari offered Rama half-eaten fruit as a sign of devotion, which he ate out of love. Later, at Panchavati, a demoness named Shurpanakha tried to seduce Rama, was rejected, and threatened Sita; Lakshmana cut off her nose and ears. Her brother, the demon king Ravana, sought revenge, saw Sita, desired her, and had his uncle Maricha lure her away disguised as a deer before kidnapping her to his island kingdom of Lanka. Rama and Lakshmana, discovering the kidnapping, traveled south, allied with the monkey king Sugriva, and gained the loyal commander Hanuman.
